questions.question: World Environment Day is celebrated on which date every year?
questions.explanation: World Environment Day has been celebrated on 5 June every year since 1974, making it the principal vehicle for the United Nations for promoting awareness and action for the environment.

questions.question: The theme for World Environment Day 2026 was:
questions.explanation: World Environment Day 2026 focused on 'Beat Plastic Pollution', urging nations and individuals to reduce plastic waste and its devastating impact on marine and terrestrial ecosystems.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution directs the state to protect and improve environment?
questions.explanation: Article 48A (Directive Principle) directs the State to protect and improve environment. Article 51A(g) (Fundamental Duty) makes it the duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment.

questions.question: The 'National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)' was launched in India in the year:
questions.explanation: India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) was launched on June 30, 2008, comprising eight national missions including Solar Mission, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, and Sustainable Agriculture.

questions.question: Which country recently achieved 100% renewable electricity for an entire month?
questions.explanation: Portugal achieved a historic milestone by running entirely on renewable energy (wind, hydro, and solar) for a full month, demonstrating the viability of 100% clean electricity for a European nation.

questions.question: The 'Green Credit Programme' in India is regulated by:
options: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.correctAnswer: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.explanation: The Green Credit Programme (GCP) is administered by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) under the Environment Protection Act 1986, incentivizing voluntary green actions.

questions.question: The Ramsar Convention is related to the conservation of:
questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. India has 75+ Ramsar sites, the largest network in Asia.

questions.question: Which Indian state has the highest number of Ramsar Wetland sites?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu has the highest number of Ramsar sites in India, reflecting its rich biodiversity of wetlands including Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary, Karikili Bird Sanctuary, and Point Calimere Wildlife Sanctuary.
